'''''Thesium humifusum''''' is a species of [[parasitic plant|hemiparasitic]] [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Santalaceae]] found in western Europe and north-western Africa, known as '''bastard-toadflax'''.

==Distribution==
Within continental Europe, ''Thesium humifusum'' is found throughout [[France]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tela-botanica.org/bdtfx-nn-67814-synthese |title=''Thesium humifusum'' |work=eFlore: L'encyclopédie botanique collaborative |publisher=[[Tela Botanica]] |accessdate=2020-07-08}}</ref> [[Spain]]<ref>{{cite book |author=J. Pedrol & M. Laínz |chapter=''Thesium'' L. |series=Flora Iberica |volume=8 |title=Haloragaceae–Euphorbiaceae |pages=152–159 |editor=Santiago Castroviejo Bolibar |year=1997 |publisher=[[Real Jardín Botánico]] |location=Madrid |isbn=84-00-07654-0}}</ref> and [[Italy]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=thesium+humifusum |title=''Thesium humifusum'' DC. |work=Flora Italiana |accessdate=2020-07-08}}</ref> In the [[Netherlands]], it is very rare, being now restricted to a single dune system near [[Katwijk aan Zee]].<ref name="FLORON">{{cite web |url=https://www.verspreidingsatlas.nl/1278 |title=''Thesium humifusum'' DC., liggend bergvlas |work=FLORON Verspreidingsatlas |publisher=NDFF |author=Niko Buiten & René van Moorsel |year=2015 |accessdate=2020-07-08}}</ref> In [[Belgium]], it can be found in coastal dunes in Flanders, and perhaps one site in Wallonia.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://wilde-planten.nl/liggend%20bergvlas.htm |title=Liggend bergvlas – ''Thesium humifusum'' |work=Wilde planten in Nederland en België |author=K. M. Dijkstra |accessdate=2020-07-08}}</ref> It is the only species of ''Thesium'' in Great Britain,<ref name="Stace"/> and is there considered 'scarce'.<ref name="Wells">{{cite book |author=T. C. E. Wells |year=1994 |chapter=''Thesium humifusum'' |title=Scarce Plants in Britain |editor=A. Stewart |editor2=D. A. Pearman |editor3=C. D. Preston |publisher=JNCC |location=Peterborough, UK |isbn=978-1873701669}}</ref> ''Thesium humifusum'' may also occur in parts of [[North Africa]].<ref name="Euro+Med">{{cite web |url=http://ww2.bgbm.org/EuroPlusMed/PTaxonDetail.asp?NameCache=Thesium%20humifusum&PTRefFk=7300000 |title=''Thesium humifusum'' DC. |work=The Euro+Med PlantBase – the information resource for Euro-Mediterranean plant diversity |publisher=[[Berlin Botanical Garden and Botanical Museum|Botanic Garden and Botanical Museum Berlin-Dahlem]] |year=2006 |accessdate=2020-07-08}}</ref>

==Ecology==
''Thesium humifusum'' is a [[Parasitic plant|hemiparasitic plant]] that steals nutrients from [[Galium album|hedge bedstraw]] (''Galium album'') or [[Galium verum|lady's bedstraw]] (''Galium verum'').<ref name="FLORON"/> Although it can be abundant in appropriate habitats, its low growth habit and inconspicuous flowers mean that it is often overlooked.<ref name="Wells"/> In Great Britain, it is restricted to [[downland]]s over [[chalk]] or [[oolitic limestone]] in southern England.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/thesium-humifusum |title=''Thesium humifusum'' |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |publisher=[[Biological Records Centre]] |accessdate=2020-07-08}}</ref> Elsewhere, it may also grow in [[dune|sand dune systems]].<ref name="FLORON"/>

==Description==
''Thesium humifusum'' usually grows flat along the ground, only occasionally producing more erect flowering stems. Its leaves are a yellowish green colour and are strap-shaped and up to {{convert|25|mm|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} long, with a single central vein. The flowers are also yellowish, and only {{convert|2|-|3|mm|abbr=on|sigfig=1}} long. They have five [[tepal]]s, five [[stamen]]s, and a single [[ovary (botany)|ovary]] with three ovules and one style.<ref name="Stace">{{cite book |author=[[Clive A. Stace]] |year=2019 |title=New Flora of the British Isles |edition=4th |publisher=C&M Floristics |isbn=978-1-5272-26302 |chapter=Santalaceae – bastard-toadflax family |pages=451–452}}</ref><ref name="FLORON"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Thesium humifusum'' was first described by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] in the 1815 third edition of his ''Flore Française''.<ref name="Euro+Med"/> In English, it is known simply as 'bastard-toadflax'.<ref name="Stace"/>
